issue_context.title: Environment.GetCommandLineArgs()[0] points to non-existing file in single-file apps
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @swaroop-sridhar, @agocke
See info in area-owners.md if you want to be subscribed.
Also, `typeof(Program).Assembly.Location` and `.CodeBase` return same absolute path to the non-existent `zzz.dll`.

@sbomer Could you take a look at this?

I'm actually not clear on what this should return. I think the user would expect the path to the single-file app, but if we don't return the path to the app host in the self-contained case it's also a little weird to do so now.

> but if we don't return the path to the app host in the self-contained case it's also a little weird to do so now.

But self-contained apps will deploy a dll that the user can actually see.
@mateoatr Right, that's why I'm leaning towards the file path of the host. It just seems like the only thing we could reasonably point to.
Actually @mateoatr could you look at this instead? I @sbomer is looking at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/36089

> I'm actually not clear on what this should return. I think the user would expect the path to the single-file app, but if we don't return the path to the app host in the self-contained case it's also a little weird to do so now.

When an app is executed using an apphost (self-contained, framework-dependent, or single-file), its intuitive to expect the host-path as `GetComandLineArgs[0]`. I'm not sure why the path to the DLL is returned in place of the host path. 

@jkotas Is this because we want to maintain consistency between runs that use `dotnet` host and apphost? 
Do we know of any tooling that depends on the fact that `GetComandLineArgs[0]` is the path to the main assembly? 

The other option is to return empty string as the assembly-path. The spec says "The first element in the array contains the file name of the executing program. If the file name is not available, the first element is equal to String.Empty."

> I'm leaning towards the file path of the host. It just seems like the only thing we could reasonably point to.

I second.

> Is this because we want to maintain consistency between runs that use dotnet host and apphost?

I believe that the code to compute the 0-th command line arg was inherited from Windows Phone, and it happened to work ok for .NET Core up until now.

> Do we know of any tooling that depends on the fact that GetComandLineArgs[0] is the path to the main assembly?

I do not aware of any app that has dependency like this. It is likely that some exists. This falls under the general single-file compatibility issues. The apps that expect their managed entrypoint .dll exists on disk will need updates for single file.

> The spec says

The spec also says: "The program file name can, but is not required to, include path information."

> I'm leaning towards the file path of the host. 

+1

review_comments:
I think it would be better to have one parametrized test asset for single-file API tests, rather than a different asset for each API. For example, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/40974 will need a test for `Assembly.CodeBase`. We also need to add tests for `Assembly.Location`, `AppContext.BaseDirectory`, etc. 

But I'm fine if we take this change, and adapt it when we test a second API.
Hi @mateoatr  these tests should be separate facts. Thanks.
Does it make sense to have the second test here? Feels a little bit weird to test the behavior of a non single-file app in this file.

I agree that this is not a great factoring. I suggested having the related test here because we have the infrastructure (and we cannot yet test single-file easily from Libraries subset). But its only a suggestion.

However, if we do keep the two versions they should be separate facts, because unit tests should test only *one* thing. Thanks for making the change.
Thanks for making the change.
Its probably a good idea to add a test for non-single-file case here, and check that we get `AppPath` -- to reinforce our understanding, given that we have the test infrastructure available.
